prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Alder Creek Electrical Distribution Substation supplies transformer/feeder bays. Bay Automation Controller (Juniper) validates authority/mode/interlocks/availability, commands/compares indications, flags discrepancies, associates Breaker Inspection Tag, uses Battery Load Test Record, sends Bay Status Digest→Station Supervisory Control System (Glasswing). Glasswing displays authorized controls/quality/staleness, retains alarms/events, produces Alarm Acknowledgement Slip, receives Protocol Retry Summary←Station Gateway (authorized mapped traffic, timestamps/quality/link errors; no equipment-state changes). Breaker Control Unit returns position/circuit-health; commands/tests cannot bypass local interlocks/authority; control failure cannot inhibit protection. North Bay Controller blocks unready closes/preserves local control during supervisory loss; South Bay Controller reports mode/availability; scopes non-substitutable. Feeder Protection Relay (Tandem) independently trips using approved settings, produces Relay Diagnostic Note; testing must preserve energized-feeder protection. North Protection Panel maintains independent zone/trip paths; Transformer Protection Panel independently protects transformers. Satellite Time Receiver (Bluefin) supplies quality-checked time/Clock Drift Snapshot→Sequence Event Archive (Orchard), retaining authoritative events/control outcomes/testing/restoration. Engineering Workstation provides authorized revision-controlled review/configuration/export, produces Settings Review Receipt→Maintenance Remote Terminal (maintenance-only; no bypass). Station DC System monitors supplies/abnormal loss, retains Battery Load Test Record. Control Room Operator requests switching, reviews/acknowledges alarms, records actions/restrictions, tracks disabled protection until verified restoration, produces Clearance Handoff Memo. Switching Desk Coordinator (Keystone) checks prerequisites/conflicts/clearances, maintains switching sequence, produces Isolation Boundary Card/confirms handback. Substation Supervisor authorizes/escalates, controls communication/mapping/logic/configuration changes, coordinates timing/responsibilities with Keystone. Protection Relay Engineer (Larkspur) reviews settings/coordination/events/test scope/restoration. Substation Field Crew (Cinder) locally verifies identity/status/boundaries, produces Breaker Inspection Tag(condition/time), reports discrepancies/unsafe conditions; work requires confirmed clearance/isolation/grounding. Requirements: plan maintenance for loading/switching/staffing; approved tests/calibrated instruments/stop means; inhibit uncertain/nonpermissive remote commands; degraded indications unavailable pending verification; manual operation requires procedures/local checks/operator communication. Preserve rejection context, bounded authority/local precedence, ordered switching/holds/stops, abnormal discrepancies, source/order/time/quality/uncertainty; time

New part:
S218: A suspected controller or relay fault is assessed before any restart, bypass, or replacement is attempted.
S219: Restoration includes confirming normal indications, protection availability, communications status, and the removal of temporary test connections.
S220: The Substation Supervisor confirms that required records are complete and that operating restrictions are formally cleared before returning equipment to normal service.
S221: Operational assurance at Alder Creek depends on clear authority, verified equipment state, and records that support later review.
S222: The Control Room Operator remains responsible for deciding whether an automation request is appropriate for current operating conditions.
S223: The Bay Automation Controller shall execute only commands permitted by its approved logic and configured interlocks.
S224: The Feeder Protection Relay shall retain its protective function independently of supervisory communications.
S225: The Protection Relay Engineer reviews protection behavior after material changes and records any unresolved concerns for operational follow-up.
S226: The Station Supervisory Control System presents control indications and command results for operator assessment.
S227: The Sequence Event Archive retains time-ordered records needed to reconstruct significant control and protection events.
S228: The Engineering Workstation shall be used for authorized configuration work under established change control.
S229: The Satellite Time Receiver supports consistent event timing, and time-quality concerns shall be investigated before records are relied upon for sequence analysis.
S230: The Station Gateway shall maintain the defined boundary between station automation and external communications.
S231: The Station DC System shall be confirmed available before switching that depends on station control power.
S232: The Breaker Control Unit shall reject commands that do not satisfy its configured permissive conditions.
S233: Substation Field Crew uses the Isolation Boundary Card to verify the approved work boundary before entering the controlled area.
S234: Substation Field Crew reports unexpected equipment conditions promptly and pauses work when the approved boundary is uncertain.
S235: Switching Desk Coordinator receives the Clearance Handoff Memo and confirms that its clearance status agrees with the active switching record.
S236: Keystone shall confirm that switching authority, equipment state, and communication limits are understood before coordinating any automation-enabled action.
S237: The Substation Supervisor verifies that unresolved risks have an assigned owner and an agreed disposition before normal service is resumed.
S238: The Control Room Operator confirms indications locally when remote status is incomplete, inconsistent, or delayed.
S239: The Protection Relay Engineer assesses unexplained trips and abnormal protection indications before protection is returned to service.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
